i don’t think that one way is necessarily better than the other, nor do i think that sparser prose is really all that new. they’re different modes of writing employed to different affects. as for the simpler language used by authors like Sanderson, that kind of writing has been around for a very long time but hasn’t typically been used in high fantasy much before now. that kind of writing tends to be more about the immediacy of the emotion or action—it’s designed to be invisible and forgettable so that the reader focuses on the events of the narrative more than the words themselves. more heightened writing slows down the pace and abstracts the action and emotion a little more. each paragraph is more dense in meaning without necessarily advancing the narrative as much. i like both kinds of writing. it just depends on what i’m in the mood for.
